symbols.name: abs
symbols.documentation: Computes the absolute value of a number or creates a abs expression. The argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: and
symbols.documentation: Computes or creates a boolean and expression with the given arguments. Each argument can be a solver expression or a boolean. It is also possible to use this function with a variadic number of arguments or with the variadic call syntax. If no argument is given, this function returns the integer 1.

symbols.name: array
symbols.documentation:
Returns an array made of the given elements (possibly arrays). Indexes begin at 0. An array doesn’t have a value by itself, but can contain operands of type boolean, integer, double, array (for multi-dimensional arrays) or collections (lists or sets). In the latter case, the collections must share the same domain and same type (either list or set). All the elements of an array must be of the same type.

When defining a variadic array (with a range or a list as the first operand and a lambda function as the second operand), we allow a recursive definition of the elements in this array by using a second argument in the function, containing the evaluation of the function on the previous element of the range. In this case, a third operand can be added, representing the value of the element before the first element in the array.

symbols.name: at
symbols.documentation:
If arr is an array:

Returns the given indexed element of array arr.

The model will be considered as infeasible while no such element exists.

If arr is a list:

Only one index can be given.

Returns the given indexed element of list arr.

The model will be considered as infeasible if the index is negative or greater or equal to count().

symbols.name: bool
symbols.documentation: Creates a new boolean decision and adds it to the Hexaly Optimizer model. This function always returns a solver expression.

symbols.name: call
symbols.documentation: Calls a function. It can be used to implement your own operator. See external functions for details.

symbols.name: ceil
symbols.documentation: Computes the ceiling of the argument or creates a ceil expression. The argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: constArray
symbols.documentation: Creates a constant array expression containing the given values. Note that the constant array created does not have operands.

symbols.name: contains
symbols.documentation: Returns true if the first operand contains the second one, false otherwise. This operator takes exactly two arguments: the first one is an interval, a collection (list() or set()), an array() of collections or a constant array, the second one either an integer expression or an interval to search for. If expr1 is an array, all its collections must be of the same type and on the same range. If expr2 is an interval, expr1 must also be an interval. In this case contains(expr1, expr2) is true if and only if the interval expr2 is fully contained in the first interval expr1. An interval I2 is considered fully contained in I1 if it starts at or after I1’s start and ends at or before I1’s end. It will then return False if the interval expr1 is void. If the interval expr2 is void this operator will return undefined.

symbols.name: cos
symbols.documentation: Computes or creates a cosine expression with the given argument. The argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: count
symbols.documentation: Returns the number of elements in an array, interval, list() or set().

symbols.name: cover
symbols.documentation: Returns an expression equal to true when all the operands form a cover of their common domain. All the operands must be collections of the same type (either list() or set()) and on the same range. These collections can be stored in a LSArray that will be passed as argument of the cover: COVER(array(c1, c2, ..., cN)).

symbols.name: disjoint
symbols.documentation: Returns an expression equal to true when all the operands are pairwise disjoint. All the operands must be collections of the same type (either list() or set()) and on the same range. These collections can be stored in a LSArray that will be passed as argument of the disjoint: DISJOINT(array(c1, c2, ..., cN)).

symbols.name: dist
symbols.documentation: Computes the distance between two numbers or creates a distance expression. Each argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: distinct
symbols.documentation: Returns the unordered set of distinct values of the given array, or among all the values returned by the function called on each element of the given collection (list() or set()), interval() or range().

symbols.name: div
symbols.documentation: Computes the division between two numbers or creates a div expression. Each argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: doubleArrayExternalFunction
symbols.documentation: Adds a custom function to the model. This funciton must return a double array. See external functions for details.

symbols.name: doubleExternalFunction
symbols.documentation: Adds a custom function to the model. This function must return a double value. See external functions for details.

symbols.name: end
symbols.documentation: Returns the end of a non-void interval.

symbols.name: eq
symbols.documentation: Compares the arguments or creates an equality solver expression. Each argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: exp
symbols.documentation: Computes or creates an exponential expression with the given argument. The argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: find
symbols.documentation: Returns the position of the first collection containing the given element in the array. If the element is not in any collections of the array, it returns -1. If the element belongs to several collections, it returns the smallest position among the collections containing the element. This operator takes exactly two arguments: the first one is an array() of collections, the second one is the element searched. All the collections of the array must be of same type and on the same range.

symbols.name: findHeader
symbols.documentation: Returns the cookie with the given name or nil if no cookie with such name exists. The name is case-sensitive. Foo or foo are considered as two different cookies.

symbols.name: float
symbols.documentation: Creates a new float decision with the given bounds [lb, ub] and adds it to the Hexaly Optimizer model. This function always returns a solver expression. Bounds must be numbers (integers or doubles).

symbols.name: floor
symbols.documentation: Computes the floor of the argument or creates a floor expression. The argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: geq
symbols.documentation: Compares the arguments or creates an inequality ‘greater than or equal to’. solver expression. Each argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: gt
symbols.documentation: Compares the arguments or creates an inequality ‘greater than’ solver expression. Each argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: hull
symbols.documentation: Operands must be interval. Intervals can be stored in a LSArray that will be passed as argument of the hull: HULL(array(i1, i2, ..., iN)) Returns the smallest interval included in all the intervals given as arguments: its start is equal to the smallest start of its arguments, and its end is equal to the largest end of its arguments. Void intervals are ignored.

symbols.name: hxIterationBetweenTicks
symbols.documentation: Interval in iterations between two iteration ticks during the search. This number must be strictly positive. Default value is 10,000.

symbols.name: hxIterationLimit
symbols.documentation:
The number(s) of iterations of Hexaly Optimizer algorithms allowed in the search. It can be an integer or a collection of integers (always non-negative). The default number of iterations is set to the largest positive integer, that is 2^63-1 = 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 > 10^18. If hxIterationLimit is set to an integer value, the search will stop after this granted amount of iterations (or earlier if an optimal solution is found). If hxIterationLimit is set to a collection of integers, then the search will proceed by phases:

the first number will be the number of iterations allocated to the optimization of the first objective (1st phase),

the second number will be the number of iterations allocated to the second objective (2nd phase),

and so on…

The number of iteration limits must be smaller or equal to the number of objectives. Note that if the optimal value of an objective is found before the end of the corresponding phase, the remaining number of iterations will be transferred to the next phase.

symbols.name: hxNbDisplayedObjectives
symbols.documentation: Maximum number of objectives to display. Default value is 7.

symbols.name: hxNbDisplayedViolatedConstraints
symbols.documentation: Maximum number of violated constraints to display. Default value is 6.

symbols.name: hxNbThreads
symbols.documentation:
Number of threads used to parallelize the search. The default value is 0, which means that the number of threads is automatically adapted to your computer and to your optimization model. When set to 0, the system will create at least 4 threads by default, as it is recommended to have at least 4 physical cores for nominal performance. This parameter is indicative, if needed Hexaly Optimizer may use more threads. The actual number of threads can also vary during the search.

Furthermore, if you use external functions with Hexaly Modeler, the optimizer will use only one thread to avoid concurrent accesses to your external function. Please read Performance issues for more details.

symbols.name: hxObjectiveThreshold
symbols.documentation:
Sets the threshold of the objective. If hxObjectiveThreshold is set to an integer or a double (according to the objective type), the optimization is stopped as soon as the lower (minimization case) or upper (maximization case) threshold is reached.

It can also be a collection of integer or doubles for multi-objectives problems.

symbols.name: hxSeed
symbols.documentation: The seed of the pseudorandom number generator used by Hexaly Optimizer internally to perform its search. This number must be positive or zero. Default value is 0.

symbols.name: hxSolution
symbols.documentation:
Gives access to the solution object of the solver. With this variable you can query the status of the solution (with hxSolution.status), the bounds and the gaps of the objectives (with hxSolution.objectiveBounds and hxSolution.objectiveGaps).

For more information on all the available fields and features of this variable, please refer to the documentation of HxSolution Class.

This variable is not available during the modeling phase. Therefore, the value of this variable during the execution of the input() and model() methods is nil.

symbols.name: hxStatistics
symbols.documentation:
Gives access to the statistics of the solver. With this variable you can query the various statistics exposed by the solver at the end of the optimization or during the optimization when the method display is periodically invoked.

The resolution time is available in hxStatistics.runningTime and the number of iterations in hxStatistics.nbIterations. For more information on all the available fields and features of this variable, please refer to the documentation of HxStatistics Class.

This variable is not available during the modeling phase. Therefore, the value of this variable during the execution of the input() and model() methods is nil.

symbols.name: hxTimeBetweenDisplays
symbols.documentation: Interval in seconds between two displays during the search. This number must be strictly positive. Default value is 1.

symbols.name: hxTimeBetweenTicks
symbols.documentation: Interval in seconds between two time ticks during the search. This number must be strictly positive. Default value is 1.

symbols.name: hxTimeLimit
symbols.documentation:
The time limit(s) allocated to the search, in seconds. It can be an integer or a collection of integers (always non-negative). Note that the “real” time (that is, total time) spent to resolve the model is considered here and not only the CPU time. The default time limit is set to the largest positive integer on 32 bits, that is 2^31-1 = 2,147,483,647 > 10^9. If hxTimeLimit is set to an integer value, the search will stop after this granted amount of seconds (or earlier if an optimal solution is found). If hxTimeLimit is set to a collection of integers, then the search will proceed by phases:

the first number will be the number of seconds allocated to the optimization of the first objective (1st phase),

the second number will be the number of seconds allocated to the second objective (2nd phase),

and so on…

The number of time limits must be smaller or equal to the number of objectives. Note that if the optimal value of an objective is found before the end of the corresponding phase, the remaining time will be transferred to the next phase.

symbols.name: hxVerbosity
symbols.documentation:
Verbosity level of the solver. The amount of information displayed during the search depends on this parameter. There are 3 different levels:

0: All traces are disabled

1: Normal verbosity. Displays only the most crucial indicators: objectives, elapsed time and number of iterations.

2: Wordy level. Displays additional statistics like the number of decisions of each type.

symbols.name: hxWarningLevel
symbols.documentation:
Controls whether warning computation is performed during preprocessing. There are 3 different levels:

0: Disable warning computation.

1: Automatic behavior - warning computation is enabled by default but may be automatically disabled for very large instances.

2: Force warning computation on all instances, including large ones.

symbols.name: iif
symbols.documentation: Performs the if or creates a ternary conditional expression. The condition can be a solver expression or a boolean. The trueValue and falseValue can be solver expressions, booleans, integers or doubles. If the condition is a boolean, trueValue or falseValue is returned accordingly without any further treatment. Otherwise a new solver expression is returned.

symbols.name: indexOf
symbols.documentation: Returns the position of the given element in a list(), or -1 if the element is not in the list. The returned value is an integer from -1 to count(list)-1

symbols.name: int
symbols.documentation: Creates a new integer decision with the given bounds [lb, ub] and adds it to the Hexaly Optimizer model. This function always returns a solver expression. Bounds must be integers.

symbols.name: intArrayExternalFunction
symbols.documentation: Adds a custom function to the model. This function must return a int array. See external function for details.

symbols.name: intExternalFunction
symbols.documentation: Adds a custom function to the model. This function must return an integer value. See external functions for details.

symbols.name: intersection
symbols.documentation:
With collection expressions Returns the intersection between an array/collection and an other array/collection. This operator accepts two operands. The operator takes a collection (set or list), or an array (constant or not) as its first and second operand. The operator returns the unordered set of the values present in both operands.

With intervals The number of operands is n >= 1. Return the biggest interval fully present in all operands.

symbols.name: interval
symbols.documentation: Creates a new interval decision included in [minStart, maxEnd) and adds it to the Hexaly Optimizer model. Start is inclusive and end is exclusive. This function always returns a solver expression. Bounds must be integers.

symbols.name: length
symbols.documentation: Returns the length of a non-void interval. The length of an interval is equivalent to end(interval) - start(interval). It differs from the count on void intervals since the length of a void interval is undefined whereas the count of a void interval is 0.

symbols.name: leq
symbols.documentation: Compares the arguments or creates an inequality ‘lower than or equal to’ solver expression. Each argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: list
symbols.documentation: Creates a new list decision that can contain integers in [0, n-1]. See lists variables for a description of list variables.

symbols.name: log
symbols.documentation: Computes or creates a natural logartihm expression with the given argument. The argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: lt
symbols.documentation: Compares the arguments or creates an inequality ‘lower than’ solver expression. Each argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: map
symbols.documentation: Creates a new map initialized with the given arguments. Keys will start at 0. You can use this function with a variadic number of arguments or with the variadic call syntax. If no argument is given, this function returns an empty map. .

symbols.name: max
symbols.documentation: Computes or creates a max expression with the given arguments. Each argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double. It is also possible to use this function with a variadic number of arguments or with the variadic call syntax, but note that at least one argument is required.

symbols.name: min
symbols.documentation: Computes or creates a min expression with the given arguments. Each argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double. It is also possible to use this function with a variadic number of arguments or with the variadic call syntax, but note that at least one argument is required.

symbols.name: mod
symbols.documentation: Computes the modulo between two integers or creates a mod expression. Each argument can be a solver expression, a boolean or an integer.

symbols.name: neq
symbols.documentation: Compares the arguments or creates a disequality solver expression. Each argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: not
symbols.documentation: Negates a boolean or creates a boolean not expression. The argument can be a solver expression or a boolean.

symbols.name: optionalInterval
symbols.documentation: Creates a new optional interval decision, which can either be absent (void) or included in [minStart, maxEnd) and adds it to the Hexaly Optimizer model. When present, start is inclusive and end is exclusive. When absent, start and end are undefined. This function always returns a solver expression. Bounds must be integers.

symbols.name: or
symbols.documentation: Computes or creates a boolean or expression with the given arguments. Each argument can be a solver expression or a boolean. It is also possible to use this function with a variadic number of arguments or with the variadic call syntax. If no argument is given, this function returns the integer 0.

symbols.name: partition
symbols.documentation: Returns an expression equal to true when all the operands form a partition of their common domain. All the operands must be collections of the same type (either list() or set()) and on the same range. These collections can be stored in a LSArray that will be passed as argument of the partition: PARTITION(array(c1, c2, ..., cN)).

parameters.name: x
parameters.doc: A non-decreasing array of ‘’n’’ constant numbers, with ‘’n’’ >= 2.

symbols.name: pow
symbols.documentation: Computes a power b or creates a pow expression. Each argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: presence
symbols.documentation: Returns the presence of an interval.

symbols.name: print
symbols.documentation: Same as println() without the new line.

symbols.name: println
symbols.documentation: Writes the arguments to the standard output followed by a new line. If an argument is not convertible to a string, an error is thrown. You can use this function with a variadic number of arguments or with the variadic call syntax. If no argument is given, this function simply prints a new empty line.

symbols.name: prod
symbols.documentation: Computes or creates a product expression with the given arguments. Each argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double. It is also possible to use this function with a variadic number of arguments or with the variadic call syntax. If no argument is given, this function returns the integer 1.

symbols.name: round
symbols.documentation: Returns the closest integer to the argument or creates a round expression. The argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: scalar
symbols.documentation: Returns the scalar product of the two arrays (of the same length).

symbols.name: set
symbols.documentation: Creates a new set decision that can contain integers in [0, n-1]. See sets variables for a description of set variables.

symbols.name: sin
symbols.documentation: Computes or creates a sine expression with the given argument. The argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: sort
symbols.documentation: Returns the input sorted in ascending order. This operator takes one argument that is either an array() or a collection (list(), set(), union(), distinct(), or intersection()). When used with a lambda as second argument, the operator will sort the input based on the values returned by the lambda. The sort operator guarantees that the order of elements having the same key is preserved, except when the object is a set. In that case, the order of elements having the same key will be determined by their ascending values.

symbols.name: sqrt
symbols.documentation: Computes or creates a square root expression with the given argument. The argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: start
symbols.documentation: Returns the start of a non-void interval.

symbols.name: stepArray
symbols.documentation: Returns a constant array with optimized memory. Both arguments must be constant arrays of equal size. indices must contain the indices in increasing order where there are value changes in the array. values must contain the values of the array within each interval of the given indices: the values located between indices[i - 1] and indices[i] will be equal to values[i].

symbols.name: sub
symbols.documentation: Computes the difference between two numbers or creates a sub expression. Each argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: sum
symbols.documentation: Computes or creates a sum expression with the given arguments. Each argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double. It is also possible to use this function with a variadic number of arguments or with the variadic call syntax. If no argument is given, this function returns the integer 0.

symbols.name: tan
symbols.documentation: Computes or creates a tangent expression with the given argument. The argument can be a solver expression, a boolean, an integer or a double.

symbols.name: union
symbols.documentation: Return the unordered set of the values present in at least one operand.

symbols.name: xor
symbols.documentation: Computes or creates a boolean xor expression with the given arguments. Each argument can be a solver expression or a boolean. It is also possible to use this function with a variadic number of arguments or with the variadic call syntax. If no argument is given, this function returns the integer 0.

symbols.name: colNames
symbols.documentation: Returns the columns names. If no column names were found or provided, nil is returned.

symbols.name: cols
symbols.documentation: Returns all columns as a map, indexed by column number. For each column, rows are indexed by number.

symbols.name: colsByName
symbols.documentation:
Returns all columns as a map, indexed by column name. For each column, rows are indexed by number.

If no column names were found or provided, this method will throw an error.

symbols.name: nbCols
symbols.documentation: Returns the number of columns.

symbols.name: nbRows
symbols.documentation: Returns the number of rows.

symbols.name: rows
symbols.documentation: Returns all rows as a map, indexed by row number. For each row, columns are indexed by column number.

symbols.name: rowsByColName
symbols.documentation:
Returns all rows as a map, indexed by row number. For each row, columns are indexed by column name.

If no column names were found or provided, this method will throw an error.

symbols.name: colNames
symbols.documentation: Returns the columns names. If no column names were found or provided, nil is returned.

symbols.name: nextRow
symbols.documentation: Read the next line of the CSV file. It returns the read row indexed by column numbers, or nil if the end of file is reached.

symbols.name: nextRowByColName
symbols.documentation:
Read the next line of the CSV file. It returns the read row indexed by column names, or nil if the end of file is reached.

If no column names were found or provided, this method will throw an error.

symbols.name: rowNumber
symbols.documentation: Returns the number of read rows.

symbols.name: date
symbols.documentation: Returns the date component of the current datetime instance. The returned object has the same date as this instance, and its time component set to midnight (00:00:00.0).

symbols.name: day
symbols.documentation: Gets the day of the month represented by this datetime instance. The day of the month is expressed as an integer between 1 and 31.

symbols.name: dayOfWeek
symbols.documentation: Gets the day of the week represented by this datetime instance. The day of the week is expressed as an integer between 1 and 7 where 1 represents Monday and 7 represents Sunday (according to ISO-8601 standard).

symbols.name: dayOfYear
symbols.documentation: Gets the day of the year represented by this datetime instance. The day of the year is expressed as an integer between 1 and 366.

symbols.name: hour
symbols.documentation: Gets the hour component of the date represented by this datetime instance. The hour component is expressed as an integer between 0 and 23.

symbols.name: millisecond
symbols.documentation: Gets the millisecond component of the date represented by this datetime instance. The millisecond component is expressed as an integer between 0 and 999.

symbols.name: minute
symbols.documentation: Gets the minute component of the date represented by this datetime instance. The minute component is expressed as an integer between 0 and 59.

symbols.name: month
symbols.documentation: Gets the month component of the date represented by this datetime instance. The month component is expressed as an integer between 1 and 12.

symbols.name: second
symbols.documentation: Gets the second component of the date represented by this datetime instance. The second component is expressed as an integer between 0 and 59.

symbols.name: year
symbols.documentation: Gets the year component of the date represented by this datetime instance.

symbols.name: addCallback
symbols.documentation:
Add a new callback for a specific event type. The callback will be called each time the given event occurs. When a callback is called, the solver is paused. You can stop the resolution from a callback, retrieve the current solution, retrieve the statistics of the solver and, in general, call all the methods marked as “allowed in state PAUSED”.

The same callback can be used for different events.

The callback must be a function accepting 0, 1 or 2 parameters that are respectively the Hexaly Optimizer environment and the type of the event. The type of the event must be a string among:

PHASE_STARTED: Event that occurs when a phase is started.

PHASE_ENDED: Event that occurs when a phase ends.

DISPLAY: Event that occurs regularly before, after and during the search to display useful information about the model and the resolution. The time between two such events can be tuned with the timeBetweenDisplays parameter.

TIME_TICKED: Event that occurs regularly during the resolution. The time between two such events can be tuned with the timeBetweenTicks parameter.

ITERATION_TICKED: Event that occurs regularly during the resolution. The number of iterations between two such events can be tuned with the iterationBetweenTicks parameter.

symbols.name: computeInconsistency
symbols.documentation: Compute an inconsistency core for this model. Only allowed in state STOPPED.

symbols.name: createPhase
symbols.documentation: Creates and adds a new phase to this Hexaly Optimizer environment. Only allowed in state STOPPED.

symbols.name: enter
symbols.documentation:
These operators are automatically called when a solver instance is used in a with statement.

enter is called at the beginning of the with statement. It sets the solver as the current solver, the one that will be used when calling the mathematical operators and the keywords minimize, maximize and constraint.

exit restores the previous solver as the current solver (or none).

symbols.name: loadEnvironment
symbols.documentation:
Import a complete environment from a file. Only allowed in state MODELING. The current model must be empty.

The only format supported is HXB.

The chosen file format is determined by the file suffix. An exception is thrown if the provided file suffix is not supported. The suffix may optionally be followed by .gz. In that case, this function uncompress the stream before reading.

symbols.name: model
symbols.documentation: Model associated to this Hexaly Optimizer environment. Once the model is created and closed, the solver can be launched with solve().

symbols.name: nbPhases
symbols.documentation: Number of phases. Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED.

symbols.name: param
symbols.documentation: Parameters of this Hexaly Optimizer environment.

symbols.name: phases
symbols.returns: map-like structure containing objects of type HxPhase.
symbols.documentation:
Phases. This field returns a readonly map-like structure containing HxPhase with the following features:

A count field to get the number of phases, e.g. phases.count().

An overloaded index [] operator to get a phase, e.g. phases[0]. The index must be between 0 and phases.count() - 1. Accessing a value outside these bounds throws an exception.

An overloaded iterator operator to iterate over the phases with a for statement.

symbols.name: removeCallback

parameters.name: type
parameters.doc: Type of the callback to remove. Must be a string among “PHASE_STARTED”, “PHASE_ENDED”, “DISPLAY”, “TIME_TICKED” or “ITERATION_TICKED”.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.doc: Callback to remove. Must be exactly the same instance as the one provided for addCallback().

symbols.documentation: Remove the callback for the given event type and previously added with addCallback().

symbols.name: saveEnvironment
symbols.documentation:
Export a complete environment or a model to a file.

Currently, this function supports 2 file formats:

HXB : with this format, the complete environment (model, parameters, solution, …) is exported. This format is useful to debug or replay a model in the same conditions. Since the produced file is binary, it offers good performance and space efficiency.

HXM : with this format, only the model is exported in the Hexaly Modeling Language. This format is useful to have a quick view of the optimization model or to perform some modifications. However, the file may be heavy for big models and the exact reproductibility is not guaranteed since the parameters from one execution to another may differ.

The chosen file format is determined by the file suffix. An exception is thrown if the provided file suffix is not supported. The suffix may optionally be followed by .gz. In that case, this function produces a compressed result (using deflate algorithm).

symbols.name: solution
symbols.documentation:
Best solution found by the solver. If the solver has not been started at least once, all the decision variables of the solution are set to 0, or to their closest bound if 0 is not part of their domain (such a solution may be infeasible).

Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED.

symbols.name: solve
symbols.documentation: Solves the model. This method returns only when the time limit, the iteration limit, the objective bounds are reached or when the method stop() is called. The model must be closed to launch the resolution.

symbols.name: state
symbols.documentation:
State of this Hexaly Optimizer environment. The returned value can be one of the following strings:

MODELING: Model is being built. This status is returned when the optimization model is not yet closed (or if it has been reopened).

RUNNING: The solve() method has been called. This value can only appear in the modeler when the solver calls an external function.

PAUSED: The solver and all its optimization algorithms are paused. This is the status of the solver when a callback is invoked.

STOPPED: State of the solver when the model is closed but not yet run or when the optimization is finished.

symbols.name: statistics
symbols.documentation: Statistics of this Hexaly Optimizer environment. Statistics are reset to zero before each resolution. Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED.

symbols.name: stop
symbols.documentation: Aborts the resolution previously launched using solve(). If no resolution was launched, this method does nothing. Solution and statistics remain valid. This method can be called in any state, notably in state RUNNING. Note that the effect of this method is not immediate. In particular when called within a callback, the resolution will not be stopped before the end of the callback.

symbols.name: asJson
symbols.documentation:
Converts the response body into JSON. Several options can be used to customize the behavior of the JSON parser. The options must be specified in a map. The supported options are detailed at the end of this page.

You can call this method regardless of the type of content returned by the server. However, the Content-type is still used to determine the encoding of the document. If no encoding is specified, utf-8 is assumed by default. Note that an error is thrown is the specified encoding is not supported. The list of supported enocdings is available in this page.

symbols.name: asText
symbols.documentation:
Converts the response body into text. This method will use the encoding specified by the server in the response (by reading the Content-type). If no encoding is specified, utf-8 is assumed by default.

This method can fail if the response is encoded using a non-supported charset. The list of supported encodings is available in this page.

symbols.name: cookies
symbols.documentation: Returns a map formatting the response cookies. Cookies are indexed from 0 to n-1. Each cookie is a map itself which follows the format detailed in a the cookies table below. The returned map is read-only.

symbols.name: findHeader
symbols.documentation: Returns the value of the first header whose name is given as an argument to this function, or nil if no header with such name exists. The name is not case-sensitive. Calling findHeader("Content-type) or findHeader("content-type") returns the same result.

symbols.name: headers
symbols.documentation: Returns a map containing the response headers. Headers are indexed from 0 to n-1. Each header is a map itself containing two fields: name and value. You’ll find more information on header formats in the table below. The returned map is read-only.

symbols.name: statusCode
symbols.documentation: Returns the status code of the HTTP response.

symbols.name: count
symbols.documentation: Returns the number of values in the array. Elements in arrays are indexed from 0 to count()-1.

symbols.name: index

parameters.name: position
parameters.doc: The considered position. Must be non negative and striclty smaller than the number of values in the array.

symbols.documentation: Indexer. Gets the value at the given position.

symbols.name: isUndefined

parameters.name: position
parameters.doc: Position of the value to query.

symbols.documentation:
Returns true if the value at the given position is undefined. A value can be undefined in 4 cases:

It is a double and its value is NaN (Not a Number).

It is an integer or boolean with no valid value (arithmetic or out of bounds exception).

It is an interval with at least one undefined bound.

It is the result of any ill-defined operation (at with out of bounds index or operations on undefined values for instance).

symbols.name: iterator
symbols.documentation: Returns an iterator than can be used within a for statement.

symbols.name: add
symbols.documentation: Adds the given value to this collection. Only allowed in state STOPPED. This function will fail if the given value is not an integer, is outside of the domain of the list or if this value is already included in this list (keep in mind that a list cannot contain twice the same value).

symbols.name: clear
symbols.documentation: Removes all values of this collection. Only allowed in state STOPPED.

symbols.name: contains

parameters.name: value
parameters.doc: Element whose presence in this collection is to be tested.

symbols.documentation: Returns true if the collection contains the given value, false otherwise. An exception will be thrown if the provided value is not an integer.

symbols.name: count
symbols.documentation: Returns the number of values in the collection. Elements in collections are indexed from 0 to count()-1.

symbols.name: index

parameters.name: position
parameters.doc: The considered position. Must be non negative and striclty smaller than the number of values in the collection.

symbols.documentation: Indexer. Gets the value at the given position.

symbols.name: iterator
symbols.documentation: Returns an iterator than can be used within a for statement.

symbols.name: add

parameters.name: other
parameters.doc: Can be a bool, an integer, a double or another HxExpression

symbols.documentation:
Returns a new expression that is the sum of the current expression and the argument other. This operator exists in two versions depending on the position of the current expression in the addition (left or right).

Note that in some cases, this operator can return one of the two operands rather than creating a new expression (sum with constant 0).

symbols.name: and

parameters.name: other
parameters.doc: Can be a bool or another HxExpression

symbols.documentation:
Returns a new expression that is the logical and of the current expression and the argument other. This operator exists in two versions depending on the position of the current expression in the product (left or right).

Note that in some cases, this operator can return one of the two operands rather than creating a new expression (logical and with constant 1 or true) or returns the HxExpression representing the constant 0 (logical and with constant 0 or false).

symbols.name: assignable
symbols.documentation: This operator is applied when the = sign is used on an HxExpression. The implemented behavior is to throw an exception. HxExpressions can only be manipulated with the <- operator.

symbols.name: context
symbols.documentation: External function context of this expression. Only set and allowed if this expression is an external function.

symbols.name: div

parameters.name: other
parameters.doc: Can be a bool, an integer, a double or another HxExpression

symbols.documentation:
Returns a new expression that is the division of the current expression and the argument other. This operator exists in two versions depending on the position of the current expression in the division (left or right).

Note that in some cases, this operator can return the left operand instead of creating a new expression if the right operand is the constant 1.

symbols.name: eq

parameters.name: other
parameters.doc: Can be a bool, an integer, a double or another HxExpression

symbols.documentation: Returns a new equal expression between the current expression and the argument other. This operator exists in two versions depdending on the position of the current expression (left or right).

symbols.name: geq

parameters.name: other
parameters.doc: Can be a bool, an integer, a double or another HxExpression

symbols.documentation: Returns a new greater or equal expression between the current expression and the argument other. This operator exists in two versions depdending on the position of the current expression (left or right).

symbols.name: gt

parameters.name: other
parameters.doc: Can be a bool, an integer, a double or another HxExpression

symbols.documentation: Returns a new strictly greater expression between the current expression and the argument other. This operator exists in two versions depdending on the position of the current expression (left or right).

symbols.name: index

parameters.name: index
parameters.doc: Can be a bool, an integer or another expression

symbols.documentation: Returns a new at expression. The current expression is used as the array and the argument as the index.

symbols.name: isArray
symbols.documentation: Returns true if this expression is an array, false otherwise. Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED.

symbols.name: isBool
symbols.documentation: Returns true if this expression is a boolean (ie 0 or 1), false otherwise. Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED.

symbols.name: isCollection
symbols.documentation: Returns true if this expression is a collection (list or set), false otherwise. Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED.

symbols.name: isConstant
symbols.documentation: Returns true if this expression is typed as constant in the model, false otherwise.

symbols.name: isConstraint
symbols.documentation: Returns true if this expression is tagged as constraint in the model, false otherwise.

symbols.name: isDecision
symbols.documentation: Returns true if this expression is typed as decision in the model, false otherwise.

symbols.name: isDouble
symbols.documentation: Returns true if this expression is a double, false otherwise. Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED.

symbols.name: isFunction
symbols.documentation: Returns true if this expression is a function, false otherwise. Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED.

symbols.name: isInt
symbols.documentation: Returns true if this expression is an integer, false otherwise. Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED. Note that a boolean is also an integer.

symbols.name: isNamed
symbols.documentation: Returns true if this expression has a name, and false otherwise.

symbols.name: isObjective
symbols.documentation: Returns true if this expression is tagged as objective in the model, false otherwise.

symbols.name: isRange
symbols.documentation: Returns true if this expression is a range, false otherwise. Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED.

symbols.name: isUndefined
symbols.documentation:
Returns true if the given expression has an undefined value in the best solution found by the solver. An expression can be undefined in 4 cases:

It is a double and its value is NaN (Not a Number).

It is an integer or boolean with no valid value (arithmetic or out of bounds exception).

It is an interval with at least one undefined bound.

It is the result of any ill-defined operation (at with out of bounds index or operations on undefined values for instance).

Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED. This method is a shortcut for HxSolution.isUndefined().

symbols.name: isViolated
symbols.documentation:
Returns true if the given expression is violated in the best solution found by the solver. An expression can be violated in 3 cases:

It is a constraint and its value is 0.

It is a double and its value is NaN (Not A Number).

It is an integer or boolean with no valid value (arithmetic or out of bounds exception).

Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED. This method is a shortcut for HxSolution.isViolated().

symbols.name: leq

parameters.name: other
parameters.doc: Can be a bool, an integer, a double or another HxExpression

symbols.documentation: Returns a new lower or equal expression between the current expression and the argument other. This operator exists in two versions depdending on the position of the current expression (left or right).

symbols.name: linkable
symbols.documentation: This operator is applied when the <- sign is used on an HxExpression. It only returns the current HxExpression, without changing anything

symbols.name: lt

parameters.name: other
parameters.doc: Can be a bool, an integer, a double or another HxExpression

symbols.documentation: Returns a new strictly lower expression between the current expression and the argument other. This operator exists in two versions depdending on the position of the current expression (left or right).

symbols.name: mod

parameters.name: other
parameters.doc: Can be a bool, an integer or another HxExpression

symbols.documentation:
Returns a new expression that is the remainder of the integer division of the current expression and the argument other. This operator exists in two versions depending on the position of the current expression in the modulo (left or right).

Note that in some cases, this operator can return the HxExpression representing the constant 0 if the right operand is the constant 1.

symbols.name: modify
symbols.documentation: This operator is called when an expression is used with one of the three special modifiers : MINIMIZE, MAXIMIZE or CONSTRAINT. It adds the expression to the list of objectives or constraints of the current model.

symbols.name: mul

parameters.name: other
parameters.doc: Can be a bool, an integer, a double or another HxExpression

symbols.documentation:
Returns a new expression that is the product of the current expression and the argument other. This operator exists in two versions depending on the position of the current expression in the product (left or right).

Note that in some cases, this operator can return one of the two operands rather than creating a new expression (product with constant 1) or returns the HxExpression representing the constant 0 (product with constant 0).

symbols.name: name
symbols.documentation:
Name of this expression or the empty string if no name has been set.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in state MODELING.

symbols.name: nbOperands
symbols.documentation: Number of operands of this expression.

symbols.name: neg
symbols.documentation: Returns a new expression that is the opposite of the current expression.

symbols.name: neq

parameters.name: other
parameters.doc: Can be a bool, an integer, a double or another HxExpression

symbols.documentation: Returns a new not equal expression between the current expression and the argument other. This operator exists in two versions depdending on the position of the current expression (left or right).

symbols.name: not
symbols.documentation: Returns a new expression that is the negative of the current expression. NOT(a) = 1 - a.

symbols.name: operands
symbols.returns: map-like structure containing objects of type HxExpression.
symbols.documentation:
This field returns a readonly map-like structure containing all the operands of this expression. The returned structure has the following features:

A count field to get the number of operands, e.g. operands.count().

An overloaded index [] operator to get a specific operand, e.g. operands[0]. The index must be between 0 and operands.count() - 1. Accessing a value outside these bounds throws an exception.

An overloaded iterator operator to iterate over the operands with a for statement.

symbols.name: operator
symbols.documentation: Operator of this expression returned as a string.

symbols.name: or

parameters.name: other
parameters.doc: Can be a bool or another HxExpression

symbols.documentation:
Returns a new expression that is the logical or of the current expression and the argument other. This operator exists in two versions depending on the position of the current expression in the product (left or right).

Note that in some cases, this operator can return one of the two operands rather than creating a new expression (logical or with constant 0 or false) or returns the HxExpression representing the constant 1 (logical or with constant 1 or true).

symbols.name: pos
symbols.documentation: Returns the same expression without change.

symbols.name: range

parameters.name: other
parameters.doc: Can be a bool, an integer, a double or another HxExpression

symbols.documentation: Returns a new range expression between the current expression and the argument other. This operator exists in two versions depdending on the position of the current expression (left or right).

symbols.name: sub

parameters.name: other
parameters.doc: Can be a bool, an integer, a double or another HxExpression

symbols.documentation:
Returns a new expression that is the substraction of the current expression and the argument other. This operator exists in two versions depending on the position of the current expression in the substraction (left or right).

Note that in some cases, this operator can return the left operand instead of creating a new expression if the right operand is the constant 0.

symbols.name: ternary

parameters.name: trueValue
parameters.doc: Can be a bool, an integer, a double or an HxExpression

parameters.name: falseValue
parameters.doc: Can be a bool, an integer, a double or an HxExpression

symbols.documentation: Returns a new if-then-else expression (also called the ternary operator). The current expression is used as the condition and the arguments as true and false values respectively.

symbols.name: value
symbols.returns: a number, an array or a collection depending on the type of the expression.
symbols.documentation:
Value of this expression in the best solution found by the solver. This method is a shortcut for HxSolution.getValue() and HxSolution.setValue().

The type of the returned value depends on the type of the expression. It can be a number if the expression has an integer or double value, an array if the expression is an array, or a collection if the expression is a list or a set decision.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in state STOPPED and queried in states PAUSED or STOPPED.

symbols.name: count
symbols.documentation: Returns the number of argument values. Arguments are indexed from 0 to count()-1.

symbols.name: index

parameters.name: position
parameters.doc: The considered position. Must be non negative and striclty smaller than the number of arguments.

symbols.documentation: Indexer. Gets the value at the given position.

symbols.name: isUndefined

parameters.name: position
parameters.doc: Position of the argument to query.

symbols.documentation:
Returns true if the argument at the given position has an undefined value. An undefined value is often the result of an illegal or impossible operation. For example, the square root of a negative number, the addition of 2 opposite infinities, accessing an array or collection outside its bounds…

Attempting to access an argument with an undefined value will raise an exception. It is therefore recommended to check whether or not each argument is undefined before accessing its value. This is particularly true during the feasibility phase, when the probability of incorrect operations is very high.

symbols.name: iterator
symbols.documentation: Returns an iterator than can be used within a for statement.

symbols.name: causes
symbols.returns: map-like structure containing objects of type HxExpression.
symbols.documentation:
This field returns a readonly map-like structure containing expressions responsible for the inconsistency of this model. The sub problem reduced to these expressions and their operands (recursively) is inconsistent. The returned structure has the following features:

A count field to get the number of expressions in the IIS, e.g. causes.count().

An overloaded index [] operator to get a specific expression, e.g. causes[0]. The index must be between 0 and causes.count() - 1. Accessing a value outside these bounds throws an exception.

An overloaded iterator operator to iterate over the causes with a for statement.

symbols.name: nbCauses
symbols.documentation: Number of expressions responsible for the inconsistency of this model. This method returns 0 if the inconsistency of the problem could not be proven.

symbols.name: contains

parameters.name: value
parameters.doc: element whose presence in this interval is to be tested.

symbols.documentation: Returns true if the interval contains the given value, false otherwise.

symbols.name: count
symbols.documentation: Returns the number of elements in the interval. A void or degenerate interval does not contain any element.

symbols.name: getEnd
symbols.documentation: Returns the end of the interval. Cannot be called on a void interval as it does not have a valid end.

symbols.name: getStart
symbols.documentation: Returns the start of the interval. Cannot be called on a void interval as it does not have a valid start.

symbols.name: isDegenerate
symbols.documentation: Returns true if the interval is degenerate. A degenerate interval is an interval with equal start and end bounds. It does not contain any element.

symbols.name: isVoid
symbols.documentation: Returns true if the interval is void. A void interval is an empty interval with no valid start or end bounds.

symbols.name: toString
symbols.documentation: Returns a string representation of the interval.

symbols.name: close
symbols.documentation:
Closes the model. Only allowed in state MODELING. When this method is called, the solver is placed in state STOPPED.

Once the model is closed, no expressions, constraints or objectives can be added or removed unless the model is reopened. The model must be closed before starting its resolution.

symbols.name: constraints
symbols.returns: map-like structure containing objects of type HxExpression.
symbols.documentation:
This field returns a readonly map-like structure containing all constraints added to this model. The returned structure has the following features:

A count field to get the number of constraints, e.g. constraints.count().

An overloaded index [] operator to get a specific constraint, e.g. constraints[0]. The index must be between 0 and constraints.count() - 1. Accessing a value outside these bounds throws an exception.

An overloaded iterator operator to iterate over the constraints with a for statement.

symbols.name: decisions
symbols.returns: map-like structure containing objects of type HxExpression.
symbols.documentation:
This field returns a readonly map-like structure containing all decisions added to this model. The returned structure has the following features:

A count field to get the number of decisions, e.g. decisions.count().

An overloaded index [] operator to get a specific decision, e.g. decisions[0]. The index must be between 0 and decisions.count() - 1. Accessing a value outside these bounds throws an exception.

An overloaded iterator operator to iterate over the decisions with a for statement.

symbols.name: expressions
symbols.returns: map-like structure containing objects of type HxExpression.
symbols.documentation:
This field returns a readonly map-like structure containing all expressions added to this model. The returned structure has the following features:

A count field to get the number of expressions, e.g. expressions.count().

An overloaded index [] operator to get a specific expression, e.g. expressions[0]. The index must be between 0 and expressions.count() - 1. Accessing a value outside these bounds throws an exception.

An overloaded iterator operator to iterate over the expressions with a for statement.

symbols.name: isClosed
symbols.documentation: Returns true if the model is closed, false otherwise.

symbols.name: nbConstraints
symbols.documentation: Number of constraints added to this model so far.

symbols.name: nbDecisions
symbols.documentation: Number of decisions added to this model so far.

symbols.name: nbExpressions
symbols.documentation: Number of expressions added to this model so far.

symbols.name: nbObjectives
symbols.documentation: Number of objectives added to this model so far.

symbols.name: nbOperands
symbols.documentation: Number of operands added to this model so far. This corresponds to the number of operands for all expressions declared in the model. It is an analog of the number of non zeros in matrix model encountered in mathematical programming: it gives an hint about the size and the density of your model.

symbols.name: objectiveDirections
symbols.returns: map-like structure containing strings MINIMIZE or MAXIMIZE.
symbols.documentation:
This field returns a readonly map-like structure containing the directions of the objectives expressed as strings (MINIMIZE or MAXIMIZE). The returned structure has the following features:

A count field to get the number of objectives, e.g. objectiveDirections.count().

An overloaded index [] operator to get a specific objective direction, e.g. objectiveDirections[0]. The index must be between 0 and objectiveDirections.count() - 1. Accessing a value outside these bounds throws an exception.

An overloaded iterator operator to iterate over the objective directions with a for statement.

symbols.name: objectives
symbols.returns: map-like structure containing objects of type HxExpression.
symbols.documentation:
This field returns a readonly map-like structure containing all objectives added to this model. The returned structure has the following features:

A count field to get the number of objectives, e.g. objectives.count().

An overloaded index [] operator to get a specific objective, e.g. objectives[0]. The index must be between 0 and objectives.count() - 1. Accessing a value outside these bounds throws an exception.

An overloaded iterator operator to iterate over the objectives with a for statement.

symbols.name: open
symbols.documentation:
Reopens the model. Only allowed in state STOPPED. When this method is called, the solver is placed in state MODELING.

In this state, the model can be modified: it is possible to add new expressions, constraints or objectives, modify expression operands, and remove existing constraints and objectives. However, existing expressions cannot be deleted.

symbols.name: removeConstraint

parameters.name: constraintIndex
parameters.doc: Index of the constraint to remove.

symbols.documentation: Removes the given expression from the list of constraints. If the expression was not constrained, this method does nothing and returns immediately. Only allowed in state MODELING.

symbols.name: removeObjective

parameters.name: objectiveIndex
parameters.doc: position of the objective to remove, must be an integer.

symbols.documentation: Removes the objective at the given position in the list of objectives. Note that the objectives created after the removed one have their index decreased by 1. Phases are not modified when an objective is removed. It is the user’s responsibility to change the objective index of each phase to keep it coherent (with HxPhase.optimizedObjective), or to disable it (with HxPhase.enabled). Only allowed in state MODELING.

symbols.name: iterationBetweenTicks
symbols.documentation:
Number of iterations between two events of type ITERATION_TICKED. The default number of iterations between ticks is set to 10,000.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in states MODELING or STOPPED.

symbols.name: iterationLimit
symbols.documentation:
Maximum number of iterations before the solver stops.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in states MODELING or STOPPED.

symbols.name: logFile
symbols.documentation: Path of the Hexaly Optimizer log file. If the path is nil, no log will be saved. To tune the logging verbosity, see verbosity.

symbols.name: nbDisplayedObjectives
symbols.documentation:
Maximum number of objectives to display.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in states MODELING or STOPPED.

symbols.name: nbDisplayedViolatedConstraints
symbols.documentation:
Maximum number of violated constraints to display.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in states MODELING or STOPPED.

symbols.name: nbThreads
symbols.documentation:
Number of threads used to parallelize the search. The number of threads must be a positive integer. The default number of threads is set to 0 which means that the number of threads is automatically adapted to your computer and to your optimization model. When set to 0, the system will create at least 4 threads by default, as it is recommended to have at least 4 physical cores for nominal performance.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in states MODELING or STOPPED.

symbols.name: objectiveThresholds
symbols.documentation:
Thresholds of the objectives. If an objective is minimized (resp. maximized), then the optimization of this objective is stopped as soon as this lower (resp. upper) threshold is reached. It can be useful for goal programming.

This field returns a readonly map-like structure with the following features:

A count field e.g. objectiveThresholds.count(). This count field is always equal to the number of objectives present in the model.

An overloaded index [] operator to get a threshold for a specific objective, e.g. objectiveThresholds[0]. The index must be between 0 and objectiveThresholds.count() - 1. Accessing a value outside these bounds throws an exception.

An overloaded iterator operator to iterate over the objective thresholds with a for statement.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be read in states PAUSED and STOPPED and write in state STOPPED.

symbols.name: seed
symbols.documentation:
Seed of the pseudo-random number generator used by the solver. The seed must be a positive integer. The default seed is set to 0.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in states MODELING or STOPPED.

symbols.name: timeBetweenDisplays
symbols.documentation:
Time in seconds between two consecutive displays in console while the solver is running. The default time between displays is set to 1 second.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in states MODELING or STOPPED.

symbols.name: timeBetweenTicks
symbols.documentation:
Time in seconds between two events of type TIME_TICKED. The default time between ticks is set to 1 second.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in states MODELING or STOPPED.

symbols.name: timeLimit
symbols.documentation:
Time limit in seconds before the solver stops.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in states MODELING or STOPPED.

symbols.name: verbosity
symbols.documentation:
Verbosity level of the solver. The default verbosity is set to 1. There are 3 defined verbosity levels:

0: All the traces are disabled.

1: Normal verbosity. This is the default level.

2: Detailed verbosity. Displays statistics during the search.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in states MODELING or STOPPED.

symbols.name: warningLevel
symbols.documentation:
Warning level of the solver. The warning computation behavior depends on this parameter. There are 3 different levels:

0: Warning computation is disabled

1: Normal level. Warning computation is enabled by default but may be automatically disabled for very large instances

2: Force warning computation on all instances, including large ones.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in states MODELING or STOPPED.

symbols.name: enabled
symbols.documentation:
Status of this phase. The solver only optimize enabled phases. Disabling a phase can be useful when an objective has been removed from the model. By default, a phase is enabled.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in states MODELING or STOPPED.

symbols.name: iterationLimit
symbols.documentation:
Number of iterations of this phase. The default number of iterations is set to the largest positive integer on 64 bits, that is 2^63-1 = 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 > 10^18.

Note that if the optimal value of an objective is found before the end of the corresponding phase, the remaining iterations will be transferred to the next phase.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in states MODELING or STOPPED.

symbols.name: optimizedObjective
symbols.documentation:
Optimized objective of this phase. When multiple objectives are declared, these objectives are optimized in lexicographic order (in the order of their declaration in the model). Thus, if k objectives 0, ..., k-1 are declared, each objective i can be optimized while maintaining the values of objectives 0, ..., i-1 previously obtained and ignoring the values of objectives i+1, ..., k-1.

By default, the optimized objective corresponds to the last objective declared in the model.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in states MODELING or STOPPED.

symbols.name: timeLimit
symbols.documentation:
Time limit of this phase in seconds. Note that the “real” time (that is, total time) spent to resolve the model is considered here and not only the CPU time). The default time limit is set to the largest positive integer on 32 bits, that is 2^31-1 = 2,147,483,647 > 10^9.

Note that if the optimal value of an objective is found before the end of the corresponding phase, the remaining time will be transferred to the next phase.

This attribute is read-write but it can only be changed in states MODELING or STOPPED.

symbols.name: clear
symbols.documentation: Clear the solution and set all decisions to zero. Only allowed in state STOPPED.

symbols.name: getValue

parameters.name: expression
parameters.doc: Expression for which you want the value

symbols.returns: a number, an array or a collection depending on the type of the expression.
symbols.documentation:
Returns the value of the given expression in this solution. The type of the returned value depends on the type of the expression. It can be a number if the expression has an integer or double value, an array if the expression is an array, or a collection if the expression is a list or a set decision.

Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED.

symbols.name: objectiveBounds
symbols.returns: map-like structure containing numbers (integers or doubles).
symbols.documentation:
Bounds computed by the solver for all objectives. This field returns a readonly map-like structure with the following features:

A count field e.g. objectiveBounds.count(). This count field is always equal to the number of objectives present in the model.

An overloaded index [] operator to get a bound for a specific objective, e.g. objectiveBounds[0]. The index must be between 0 and objectiveBounds.count() - 1. Accessing a value outside these bounds throws an exception.

An overloaded iterator operator to iterate over the objective bounds with a for statement.

If the solver has never been launched or if no bound was found for a particular objective, an infinite or a very large number is returned.

Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED.

symbols.name: objectiveGaps
symbols.documentation:
Gaps computed by the solver for all objectives. This field returns a readonly map-like structure with the following features:

A count field e.g. objectiveGaps.count(). This count field is always equal to the number of objectives present in the model.

An overloaded index [] operator to get a bound for a specific objective, e.g. objectiveGaps[0]. The index must be between 0 and objectiveGaps.count() - 1. Accessing a value outside these bounds throws an exception.

An overloaded iterator operator to iterate over the objective gaps with a for statement.

The gap for feasible solutions is defined as:

Infeasible solutions have an infinite gap.

Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED.

symbols.name: setValue

parameters.name: value
parameters.doc: Value assigned to the decision in this solution.

symbols.documentation:
Sets the value of the given expression in this solution. Only decisions can be set. The value must be an integer or a double depending on the type of the decision to set. If you want to modify the decisions of type collection (set or list), you should directly modify the collection returned by the method getValue().

If the solver was not launched, this value will be used as an initial value for the decision. Only allowed in state STOPPED.

symbols.name: status
symbols.returns: a string among INCONSISTENT, INFEASIBLE, FEASIBLE or OPTIMAL.
symbols.documentation:
Status of the solution. Only allowed in states PAUSED or STOPPED. The returned value can be one of the following strings:

INCONSISTENT: Solution and model are inconsistent. The solver was able to prove that the model admits no feasible solution. Note that even a model without any constraint can be inconsistent, because some computations can yield undefined results. For instance, computing, SQRT(x) with negative x yields an undefined value, which causes the solution to be invalid if it is used in an objective or a constraint (directly or indirectly).

INFEASIBLE: Solution is infeasible (some constraints are violated).

FEASIBLE: Solution is feasible but optimality was not proven.

OPTIMAL: Solution is optimal (all objective bounds are reached).

symbols.name: nbIterations
symbols.documentation:
Number of iterations.

This attribute is read-only and can only be queried in states PAUSED or STOPPED.

symbols.name: runningTime
symbols.documentation:
Running time in seconds. Note that is the “real” time spent (and not only the CPU or system time).

This attribute is read-only and can only be queried in states PAUSED or STOPPED.

symbols.name: add
symbols.documentation: Adds the given value in the map with key equals to the largest integer key presents in the map plus one or zero if no integer key exists.

symbols.name: count
symbols.documentation: Counts the number of values in the map.

symbols.name: keys
symbols.documentation: Returns the keys of the map in a new map.

symbols.name: values
symbols.documentation: Returns the values of the map in a new map.

symbols.name: init
symbols.documentation: Re-initializes the random generator with the given seed or a new seed. The seed is optional. If seed is omitted, the current system time is used to initialize the generator.

symbols.name: next
symbols.documentation: Returns the next random integer N such that a <= N < b for a <= b and b < N <= a for b < a. The generated numbers are uniformly distributed between the open range induced by a and b.

symbols.name: nextLogNormal

parameters.name: sigma
parameters.doc: Standard deviation. Must be greather than 0.

symbols.documentation: Log normal distribution.

symbols.name: nextNormal
symbols.documentation: Normal distribution.

symbols.name: nextUniform
symbols.documentation:
Returns the next floating point number N such that a <= N < b for a <= b and b < N <= a for b < a. The generated numbers are uniformly distributed between the open range induced by a and b.

This method generates floats with 52 bits of precision on the mantissa.

symbols.name: close
symbols.documentation: Closes the current stream. If the stream is already closed, do nothing. Note that one once no more value refers to a stream, it is automatically closed.

symbols.name: eof
symbols.documentation: Returns true if the end of file is reached.

symbols.name: read
symbols.documentation: Reads ands returns up to n characters in the stream as a string. The returned string can have less than n characters if the end of the stream is reached before.

symbols.name: readDouble
symbols.documentation: Reads and returns the next floating-point number available in the stream. After calling this function, the stream cursor is positioned at the next non whitespace character or at the end of the stream if the remaining characters contains only whitespaces (see string.isWhitespace() for the definition of a whitespace). If the read sequence cannot be converted to a valid integer, an error is thrown. If the stream is already positioned at the end-of-file or is not readable, an error is thrown.

symbols.name: readInt
symbols.documentation: Reads and returns the next integer available in the stream. After calling this function, the stream cursor is positioned at the next non whitespace character or at the end of the stream if the remaining characters contains only whitespaces (see string.isWhitespace() for the definition of a whitespace). If the read sequence cannot be converted to a valid integer, an error is thrown. If the stream is already positioned at the end-of-file or is not readable, an error is thrown.

symbols.name: readString
symbols.documentation: Reads and returns the next sequence of non whitespace characters. After calling this function, the stream cursor is positioned at the start of the next string or at the end of the stream if the remaining characters contains only whitespaces (see string.isWhitespace() for the definition of a whitespace). If the file is already positioned at the end-of-file or is not readable, an error is thrown.

symbols.name: readln
symbols.documentation: Reads ands returns the next line in the stream. After calling this function, the stream cursor is positioned at the start of the next line or at the end of the stream if no characters are available. If the stream is not readable or if no line is available, an error is thrown. Note that the line terminator is trimmed and is not returned.

symbols.name: close
symbols.documentation: Closes the current stream. If the stream is already closed, do nothing. Note that one once no more value refers to a stream, it is automatically closed.

symbols.name: flush
symbols.documentation: Flush the stream. Useful for buffered streams.

symbols.name: print
symbols.documentation: Writes the arguments in the stream. The values will be converted to strings. If an argument is not convertible to a string, an error is thrown. Arguments are written without space or special formatting.

symbols.name: println
symbols.documentation: Same as print() but adds a new line in the stream.

symbols.name: endsWith
symbols.documentation: Returns true if the string ends with the given suffix. If the suffix is an empty string, returns true.

symbols.name: indexOf

parameters.name: start
parameters.doc: The position to start the search from. If the start position is negative, an exception is thrown.

symbols.documentation: Returns the first position of the substring search in the string. If no start position is given, the search starts at the beginning of the string. Returns -1 if the substring is not found.

symbols.name: isDigit
symbols.documentation: Returns true if the string contains only digits and there is at least one character, false otherwise. A character is a digit only it its unicode general category is “Number, Digit” (Nd). “0123456789” are examples of digits.

symbols.name: isLetter
symbols.documentation:
Returns true if the string contains only letters and there is at least one character, false otherwise. A character is a letter only if its unicode general category is any of the following:

Letter, Uppercase (Lu)

Letter, Lowercase (Ll)

Letter, Titlecase (Lt)

Letter, Modifier (Lm)

Letter, Other (Lo)

symbols.name: isLower
symbols.documentation: Returns true if the string contains only characters that are lowercase and there is at least one character, false otherwise. A character is lowercase only if its unicode general category is “Letter, Lowercase” (Ll).

symbols.name: isSpace
symbols.documentation:
Returns true if the string contains only spaces and there is at least one character, false otherwise. A character is a space only if its unicode general category is any of the following:

Separator, Space (Zs)

Separator, Line (Zl)

Separator, Paragraph (Zp)

The definitions of “spaces” and “whitespaces” are quite similar, and a space is also a whitespace. But whitespaces also include special control characters like “\n” or “\t” that are not labeled as “spaces” by the unicode consortium. Read isWhitespace() for more details.

symbols.name: isUpper
symbols.documentation: Returns true if the string contains only characters that are uppercase and there is at least one character, false otherwise. A character is uppercase only if its unicode general category is “Letter, Uppercase” (Lu).

symbols.name: isWhitespace
symbols.documentation:
Returns true if the string contains only whitespaces and there is at least one character, false otherwise. A character is a space only if it has the property “WSpace=Y” in the unicode database. The complete list of whitespaces contains:

All characters with general category “Separator, Space” (Zs)

All characters with general category “Separator, Line” (Zl)

All characters with general category “Separator, Paragraph” (Zp)

The control character “Horizontal tabulation” (U+0009)

The control character “Line feed” (U+000A)

The control character “Vertical tabulation” (U+000B)

The control character “Form feed” (U+000C)

The control character “Carriage return” (U+000D)

The control character “Next line” (U+0085)

symbols.name: length
symbols.documentation: Returns the length of the string as integer.

symbols.name: replace

parameters.name: search
parameters.doc: Search string. Throws an exception if this argument is empty.

symbols.documentation: Return a copy of the string with all occurrences of substring search replaced by replace.

symbols.name: split

parameters.name: delimiter
parameters.doc: Delimiter used to split the string. This parameter is optionnal. If no delimiter is provided, whitespaces are used by default.

symbols.documentation:
Returns a map that contains the substrings of this string object that are delimited by the given delimiter. For example "a::b::::c".split("::") returns {"a", "b", "", "c"}.

If no delimiter is provided, whitespaces are used as delimiter. In that case, consecutive whitespaces are considered as a single separator. Thus a string composed of whitespaces only, always returns an empty map {}. See isWhitespace() for the exact definition of a whitespace.

Splitting an empty string with or without a delimiter always returns an empty map {}.

symbols.name: startsWith
symbols.documentation: Returns true if the string starts with the given prefix. If the prefix is an empty string, returns true.

symbols.name: substring

parameters.name: start
parameters.doc: Start position. If the start position is negative or greater than the length of the string, an exception is thrown.

parameters.name: length
parameters.doc: Length of the substring (optionnal). If the given length is negative, an exception is thrown.

symbols.documentation:
Returns a new string that is a substring of this string. There are two versions of this method:

In the first version, the method takes one argument. In that case, the returned substring starts at the given position and goes to the end of the string.

In the second version, the returned substring starts at the given position and goes to the character at position start + length - 1.

symbols.name: toDouble
